questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$ and $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}\}$. Which argument proves that $V$ is a closed set?
options: $V$ is convex, and every convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is closed, so $V$ is closed as well.
Each row gives a closed set, and $V$ is the union of these $m$ closed sets, so $V$ is closed.
Each row gives a closed set, and $V$ is the intersection of these $m$ closed sets, so $V$ is closed.
$V$ is cut out by finitely many flat cuts, so it is bounded, hence compact and therefore closed.

questions.question: Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}\}$, where the $i$-th row of $\boldsymbol{A}$ is the zero vector, so that the $i$-th constraint reads $0x_1+\dots+0x_n\leq b_i$. How does this constraint affect $V$?
options: It removes nothing if $b_i\geq0$, and it makes $V$ empty if $b_i<0$.
It removes nothing for any $b_i$, since $0x_1+\dots+0x_n=0$ for every $\boldsymbol{x}$.
It makes $V$ empty if $b_i>0$, and it removes nothing if $b_i\leq0$.
It makes $V$ non-polyhedral, since a zero row does not give a halfspace.

questions.question: Let $U=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1+x_2<1\}$, a strict halfspace. Which statement about whether $U$ is a polyhedral convex set is correct?
options: $U$ is polyhedral: it is given by the single row $(1,1)$ with right-hand side $1$, and $(1,1)\neq\boldsymbol{0}$.
$U$ is not polyhedral, because it is unbounded, whereas polyhedral sets are bounded.
$U$ is not polyhedral, because a strict inequality destroys convexity.
$U$ is not polyhedral, because it is convex but not closed, whereas polyhedral sets are closed.

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$ and $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}\}$. Which statement about how small or large $V$ can be is correct?
options: $V$ is nonempty whenever every row of $\boldsymbol{A}$ is nonzero, since each such row gives a nonempty halfspace.
$V$ can be empty, and it can be all of $\mathbb{R}^n$, depending on the choice of $\boldsymbol{A}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}$.
$V$ is never all of $\mathbb{R}^n$, since each of the $m$ rows cuts away part of the space.
$V$ is empty whenever $m>n$, since a system with more rows than unknowns has no solution.

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{a}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $c\in\mathbb{R}$. How can the equation $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=c$ be included in a system $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$ that describes a polyhedral set, for every value of $c$?
options: As the single row $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq c$, since the equation is the boundary case of that row.
It cannot: a system $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$ contains only inequalities, so equations are excluded.
As the two rows $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq c$ and $-\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq-c$.
As the two rows $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq c$ and $-\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq c$.

questions.question: Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1+2x_2\leq6,\ 3x_1-x_2\leq4,\ -x_1\leq1\}$. Which of the following points lies in $V$?

The set $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^4\colon x_1+2x_3\leq5,\ x_2-x_4\leq0\}$ is written as $\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}\}$ with $\boldsymbol{x}=(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)$. Which row vector is the first row of $\boldsymbol{A}$?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}1&2\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2&0&5\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: The feasible region $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1+3x_2\leq6,\ x_1\geq0,\ x_2\geq0\}$ of a linear program is to be written as $\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}\}$. Which pair $(\boldsymbol{A},\boldsymbol{b})$ does this?
options: $\boldsymbol{A}=\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\-1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$, $\boldsymbol{b}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\0\\0\end{pmatrix}$
$\boldsymbol{A}=\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $\boldsymbol{b}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\0\\0\end{pmatrix}$
$\boldsymbol{A}=\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, $\boldsymbol{b}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\0\end{pmatrix}$
$\boldsymbol{A}=\begin{pmatrix}-1&-3\\1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $\boldsymbol{b}=\begin{pmatrix}-6\\0\\0\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: Each of the following subsets of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is given by two linear inequalities. Which of them is empty?
options: $\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon x_1-x_2\leq1,\ -x_1+x_2\leq-1\}$
$\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon x_1-x_2\leq-1,\ x_1+x_2\leq-2\}$
$\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon x_1-x_2\leq1,\ -x_1+x_2\leq-2\}$
$\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon x_1-x_2\leq1,\ -x_1+x_2\leq2\}$

questions.question: Each of the following sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is polyhedral. Which of them is bounded?
options: $\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon x_1\geq0,\ x_2\geq0,\ x_1+x_2\leq3\}$
$\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon x_1+x_2\leq3,\ x_1-x_2\leq3\}$
$\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon 0\leq x_1\leq3\}$
$\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon x_1\geq0,\ x_2\geq0,\ x_1-x_2\leq3\}$

questions.question: The set $P=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_2\geq x_1^2\}$ equals the intersection of the closed halfspaces $\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon 2ax_1-x_2\leq a^2\}$ over all $a\in\mathbb{R}$. Which statement about $P$ is correct?
options: $P$ is polyhedral, since it is an intersection of closed halfspaces, each given by one row.
$P$ is not closed, since an intersection of infinitely many closed sets need not be closed.
$P$ is not convex, since its boundary parabola is curved rather than made of flat pieces.
$P$ is closed and convex, but it is not polyhedral, since finitely many rows never suffice.

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$, $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}\}$ and $\boldsymbol{p}\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Which description of $V+\boldsymbol{p}=\{\boldsymbol{x}+\boldsymbol{p}\colon\boldsymbol{x}\in V\}$ holds for every such $\boldsymbol{A}$, $\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{p}$?
options: $V+\boldsymbol{p}=\{\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{y}\leq\boldsymbol{b}\}$, since a translation leaves the rows unchanged.
$V+\boldsymbol{p}=\{\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{y}\leq\boldsymbol{b}+\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{p}\}$, again a polyhedral set.
$V+\boldsymbol{p}=\{\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}(\boldsymbol{y}+\boldsymbol{p})\leq\boldsymbol{b}\}$, again a polyhedral set.
$V+\boldsymbol{p}=\{\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{y}\leq\boldsymbol{b}+\boldsymbol{p}\}$, again a polyhedral set.

questions.question: Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}\}$, and let $W$ be the set obtained by adding one more row $\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq d$, with $\boldsymbol{c}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $d\in\mathbb{R}$, to the system. Which statement comparing $W$ with $V$ is correct?
options: $W\subseteq V$; equality is possible when the new row is redundant, and $W$ may be empty while $V$ is not.
$W$ is a proper subset of $V$, since an additional row always cuts away some points of $V$.
If $V$ is unbounded, then so is $W$, since one extra row cannot bound a set that the others leave unbounded.
$W$ is not polyhedral when $\boldsymbol{c}$ is parallel to a row of $\boldsymbol{A}$, since parallel rows conflict.

questions.question: Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1+x_2\leq4,\ x_1-x_2\leq2,\ x_2\leq\frac{1}{2}\}$. The boundary lines $x_1+x_2=4$ and $x_1-x_2=2$ of the first two rows meet in a point $\boldsymbol{p}$. Which statement about $\boldsymbol{p}$ is correct?
options: $\boldsymbol{p}=(3,1)$, and $\boldsymbol{p}\in V$, since it satisfies the first two rows with equality.
$\boldsymbol{p}=(1,3)$, and $\boldsymbol{p}\notin V$, since it violates the row $x_2\leq\frac{1}{2}$.
$\boldsymbol{p}=(3,1)$, and $\boldsymbol{p}\notin V$, since it violates the row $x_2\leq\frac{1}{2}$.
$\boldsymbol{p}=(3,-1)$, and $\boldsymbol{p}\in V$, since it satisfies all three rows.

questions.question: Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon\max\{x_1-x_2,\ 2x_2\}\leq4\}$. Which statement about $V$ is correct?
options: $V$ is not polyhedral, since $\max\{x_1-x_2,\ 2x_2\}$ is not a linear function of $\boldsymbol{x}$.
$V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon x_1+x_2\leq8\}$, the single row obtained by adding the two expressions.
$V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon x_1-x_2\leq4\}\cup\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon 2x_2\leq4\}$, a union of two halfspaces.
$V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon x_1-x_2\leq4,\ 2x_2\leq4\}$, a polyhedral set with two rows.

questions.question: Let $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1+x_2\leq2,\ -x_1+x_2\leq2\}$, which contains $\boldsymbol{0}$. For which direction $\boldsymbol{d}$ does the whole ray $\{t\boldsymbol{d}\colon t\geq0\}$ lie in $V$?
options: $\boldsymbol{d}=(1,0)$
$\boldsymbol{d}=(0,-1)$
$\boldsymbol{d}=(1,1)$
$\boldsymbol{d}=(-1,1)$

questions.question: Let $n\geq2$ and let $V_1$ and $V_2$ be polyhedral convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Which statement about the union $V_1\cup V_2$ is correct?
options: It is polyhedral for some choices, such as $\{x_1\leq0\}\cup\{x_1\geq0\}=\mathbb{R}^n$, but not for all choices.
It is always polyhedral: stacking the rows of both systems into one system describes $V_1\cup V_2$.
It is never polyhedral unless one of the sets $V_1$ and $V_2$ contains the other one.
It is polyhedral whenever $V_1\cap V_2\neq\varnothing$, since overlapping convex sets have a convex union.

questions.question: Let $n\geq2$. What is the smallest number $m$ of rows for which some $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$ make $V=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}\}$ nonempty and bounded?
options: $m=n$, since $n$ rows with linearly independent normal vectors already fix a corner point.
$m=2n$, since every coordinate needs both a lower bound and an upper bound.
$m=1$, since a zero row with $b_1<0$ already gives a bounded set.
$m=n+1$, since $n$ rows always leave a ray inside a nonempty $V$.

questions.question: For $c\in\mathbb{R}$ let $V_c=\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon x_1+x_2\leq2,\ x_1\geq0,\ x_2\geq0,\ x_1-x_2\geq c\}$. For which values of $c$ is the polyhedral set $V_c$ nonempty?
options: Exactly for $c\leq0$
Exactly for $c\leq2$
Exactly for $c\geq-2$
Exactly for $c<2$

questions.question: Let $W=\bigcap_{k=1}^{\infty}\{\boldsymbol{x}\in\mathbb{R}^2\colon 1-\frac{1}{k}\leq x_1+x_2\leq1\}$, an intersection of infinitely many sets. Which statement about $W$ is correct?
options: $W$ is not polyhedral, since its description uses infinitely many halfspaces.
$W=\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon 0\leq x_1+x_2\leq1\}$, the set for $k=1$, and it is polyhedral.
$W=\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon x_1+x_2=1\}$, which is polyhedral with two rows.
$W=\{\boldsymbol{x}\colon x_1+x_2=1\}$, which is not polyhedral, as a line has no interior points.
